matchupOfTheWeek.title: Rush Offense vs. Run Defense
matchupOfTheWeek.description: Our rush offense grades 55/100 (about average) against CHI's run defense at 13/100 (among the NFL's worst) — the widest statistical edge on the board this week.

previewTake: The Patriots head to Soldier Field for a Thursday night showdown with a Chicago defense that, on paper, looks like a piñata waiting to be whacked — specifically their run defense grading a putrid 13/100, which happens to be the widest statistical edge on this week's board against New England's respectable 55/100 rushing attack. Drake Maye's been slinging it with authority (three TDs in last week's win over the Jets), and our pass offense grades above average at 65/100, but here's the rub: the Bears are trotting out a pass rush that grades 94/100, which is among the league's elite, and our pass protection sits at 61/100 — so there's real tension between opportunity and risk. Throw in that A.J. Brown is working through a high ankle sprain and just dropped three passes in his return, and Romeo Doubs took a hit on that 42-yard TD catch against New York, and we're looking at a receiving corps that might not be operating at full strength. The good news: we're 4-1 against Chicago in the last five meetings and riding a three-game winning streak with slightly better recent form than our hosts — but this is a road night game where one specific vulnerability (the pass rush) could really hurt.
